title: Paloma and the Promise
premise: Lior Blackwood, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter scraping out a living as a part-time novelist, agrees to pose as the partner of a stranger—mysterious archivist Wren Vale—at a family reunion to escape her aunts' pity. But Wren is not who they seem: they are the child of a man wrongfully imprisoned a decade ago, and Lior's own family holds the evidence that could free him. As their fake romance turns devastatingly real, Lior must choose between protecting the grandmother she loves and delivering the confession that has been rehearsed for ten years. In the end, justice arrives not through courts but through truth spoken aloud, and Lior and Wren earn the second chance neither believed they deserved.
about_author: Odile Almeida is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing other people's confessions before writing her own stories. She lives on a windswept coast with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy collection of tide charts.

chapters.title: The Salt in the Ink
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On the eve of the Blackwood family reunion, Lior finishes a rejection-letter-riddled manuscript in her grandfather's old lighthouse cottage, broke and dreading her aunts' questions about her loveless life. The beat: loneliness sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives in the coastal town of Gullhaven under a false name, carrying a decade of research and one photograph. They watch Lior argue with a fishmonger and decide she might be the key. The beat: cold purpose warmed by unexpected curiosity.

chapters.title: The Proposition
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Wren offers Lior a deal: be their date for the reunion weekend, and they'll pay enough to save the crumbling lighthouse from sale. Lior, suspicious but desperate, agrees. The beat: transactional hope masking mutual wariness.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over cheap wine, Lior and Wren invent a meet-cute, practice hand-holding, and trade lies that feel uncomfortably close to truths. Wren almost slips about why they really came. The beat: flirtation as camouflage.

chapters.title: Arrival at Blackwood House
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The reunion begins at the family estate; Aunt Marguerite interrogates Wren over sherry while Grandmother Odette watches silently from the stairs. Lior notices Odette's hands tremble at Wren's surname alias. The beat: dread beneath the crystal.

chapters.title: Dessert and Detonation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. By dessert the fake relationship feels too real—until Wren sees the portrait above the mantel: Judge Edmund Blackwood, the man who sentenced their father. Wren's cover story nearly cracks. The beat: desire colliding with buried rage.

chapters.title: What Odette Knows
chapters.summary: Odette's POV (first of three). Late at night, Odette recognizes something in Wren's eyes—their father's eyes—and remembers the night ten years ago when she burned a letter. The beat: guilt resurfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: The Cliff Walk
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior and Wren walk the cliff path; Wren deflects questions about their past, and Lior catches them photographing the estate's study window. First real kiss, immediately regretted by both. The beat: intimacy tangled with betrayal.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback: twelve-year-old Wren at their father's trial, watching Edmund Blackwood dismiss exculpating evidence with a yawn. The promise made at the prison gates. The beat: grief forged into mission.

chapters.title: The Locked Study
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior finds Wren picking the study lock at 2 a.m. and demands answers; Wren reveals only fragments—that Edmund ruined an innocent man. Lior defends her family's honor and storms out. The beat: loyalty tested against instinct.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Aunt Marguerite, keeper of family secrets, suspects Wren is a journalist and begins digging into their background, uncovering the name Vale doesn't match any records. The beat: quiet menace.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A storm strands everyone at the estate; the power fails, and by candlelight Lior and Wren talk honestly for the first time—her failed novel, his (their) dead parent. Walls lower. The beat: vulnerability as surrender.

chapters.title: The Confession Draft
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren works on the sentence they've rehearsed for a decade—the accusation they will speak aloud to Edmund Blackwood—but keeps rewriting it, because saying it means the mission ends. The beat: fear of completion.

chapters.title: Odette's Letter
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Odette retrieves the half-burned letter from a Bible hollow: proof Edmund suppressed evidence to protect his career. She cannot decide whether to destroy it or deliver it. The beat: conscience at war with love.

chapters.title: Family Games
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Reunion games force Lior and Wren to perform couplehood publicly; the performance stops feeling fake mid-charade, witnessed by cousin Theo, who pulls Lior aside to warn her about 'that stranger.' The beat: joy shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: Theo's Warning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, a paralegal, recognized Wren's face from case files he once photocopied—the convicted man's child, all grown up. He gives Lior twenty-four hours to get the truth or he calls security. The beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Staircase
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior corners Wren; Wren finally tells everything—the wrongful conviction, the suppressed evidence, Edmund's role. Lior refuses to believe it and runs to her grandmother. The beat: world tilted off its axis.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Silence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior asks Odette directly if Edmund was capable of it. Odette's non-answer is an answer. Lior spends the night rereading her grandfather's old trial clippings. The beat: faith cracking open.

chapters.title: The Archive Box
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren breaks into the estate archive and finds the box labeled with the case number—empty except for a receipt signed by Odette Blackwood, dated the week after the trial. The beat: the trail bending toward someone unexpected.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Did
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Odette recalls how her husband, the lighthouse keeper, witnessed the real crime and gave his testimony to Edmund—who buried it. The letter she burned contained the husband's sworn statement. The beat: complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Allies of Necessity
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Lior finds Wren and, instead of turning them in, asks what she can do. They form an uneasy alliance: find the original statement before the reunion ends Sunday noon. The beat: enemies becoming partners.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Search
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following Odette's habits, Lior searches the boathouse where her grandfather kept records; they find a hidden compartment—empty, recently disturbed. Someone got there first. The beat: hope snatched away.

chapters.title: Marguerite Makes Her Move
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite confronts Wren with printed background checks and offers a bargain: leave quietly and she'll bury what she knows. Wren realizes Marguerite has the missing papers. The beat: corruption wearing pearls.

chapters.title: The Price of Protection
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior discovers Marguerite has kept the evidence for years—not from loyalty, but leverage over Edmund's estate and the family fortune. Lior realizes her whole inheritance is built on a lie. The beat: disillusionment as inheritance.

chapters.title: Saturday Night Fire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A fire breaks out in the east wing—Marguerite destroying the evidence rather than be blackmailed herself. Wren runs into the smoke. The beat: desperation outrunning caution.

chapters.title: Smoke and Ashes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior drags a coughing Wren out; most of the papers are ash, but a single water-stained page survives—half a signature, half a statement. Enough to point somewhere. The beat: ruin yielding one thread.

chapters.title: The Half Page
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Deciphering the fragment by firelight, they realize the full statement was deposited decades ago with the harbor master's office—her grandfather's second job. The beat: the past leaving a map.

chapters.title: Harbor Master's Vault
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At dawn, the current harbor master—an old friend of Grandfather—opens the legacy vault. Inside: the complete sworn statement naming the true culprit and Edmund's suppression. The beat: truth recovered from salt and rust.

chapters.title: Sunday Noon
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The reunion's final brunch. Wren stands before the assembled family, beside Lior, and speaks the rehearsed sentence at last: 'Edmund Blackwood destroyed my father to protect himself.' Silence like a held breath. The beat: the decade-long promise kept.

chapters.title: The Family Fractures
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs briefly. Edmund's widow denies; Theo corroborates with his legal knowledge; Marguerite, cornered, confesses her hoarding; Odette rises and confirms everything. The beat: a dynasty cracking along its fault lines.

chapters.title: Odette's Own Sentence
chapters.summary: Odette's POV. Odette publicly takes responsibility—for burning the letter, for silence bought with comfort—and hands Lior the surviving pages. 'Justice delayed is still justice,' she says. The beat: redemption through admission.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lawyers, reporters, and the slow machinery of exoneration begin. Wren prepares to leave, believing the mission's end means their end. Lior lets them walk to the dock without stopping them. The beat: love afraid to ask.

chapters.title: The Empty Cottage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren sits in a bus shelter with a one-way ticket, rereading Lior's novel draft found in the boathouse—a story about a lighthouse keeper waiting for someone who never comes home. The beat: recognition as heartbreak.

chapters.title: Exoneration Day
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Months later, the conviction is vacated in a small courtroom. Wren's father, freed and frail, asks only one question: 'Was there anyone good there?' Wren answers honestly. The beat: grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse For Sale
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With settlement money from the family estate divided, Lior buys the lighthouse outright and finishes her novel, changing the ending. She writes Wren a letter and mails it to a forwarding address that may not exist. The beat: hope as an act of faith.

chapters.title: Return Tide
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren returns to Gullhaven, ostensibly to thank the harbor master, actually unable to stay away. They find the lighthouse lamp lit and Lior on the gallery rail. The beat: courage arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Second Chances
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the lighthouse balcony, Lior says the line she's rehearsed since Wren left: 'I believe you now. I believe in you.' They begin again—not fake, not performance, just two people choosing each other. The beat: the promise renewed.

chapters.title: What the Light Keeps
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Lior's POV. One year later: the published novel dedicated to 'the ones who waited,' Wren's father visiting the coast, Odette planting a garden as penance and peace. The lamp turns. The beat: earned light after long dark.
